cases.name: enable-write-checkpoint
cases.notes: §5.12: `history enable --provider git` on a repository born disabled (`capabilities: { history: false }` — the state the full composition needs; the `git` composition creates every repository so). The enable appends the baseline feed row (`import`, `history enabled`, a `changed` entry per live document) and writes ONE git commit of the full current tree under it: subject `history enabled`, trailers `omgbase-seq: ep_0:2`, `omgbase-ts`, `omgbase-commit: c_2`, `omgbase-origin: import`, `omgbase-rescan: ep_0:2`, one `omgbase-doc: <id> <path> <head>` per document; the outcome carries `provider: "git"`, the baseline's commit and document count and the branch `tip`. The edit of `a.md` (c_3, head r_2) writes no history row — the feed alone; the checkpoint at 10:03 turns that row into one commit (`committed 1`, `from_seq`/`to_seq` 3) whose tree carries the new `a.md` blob and whose trailers name the row, its origin and the document's new head. No native table is written (every history projection `[]`); the manifest row's config is the git provider's.

cases.name: crash-gap-closed-by-replay
cases.notes: §5.12 / §9.7 `git.commit`: the worker writes the blobs, the tree and the commit object, then the fault site fires before `update-ref` — the checkpoint step records the error, the branch tip is still the baseline (the `git_log` after it shows one commit), the objects dangle. The next run resumes from the tip's `omgbase-seq` trailer, rebuilds the same commit byte for byte (same tree, same message, same dates and identity → the same sha) and moves the ref: the gap between the database commit and the git commit is closed by replay, idempotently.

cases.name: purge-removes-the-repository-and-a-checkpoint-rescans
cases.notes: §7.6 on a git-provider repository: `history purge` deletes the bare repository and the worker's `$git` cursor row (`provider: { name: "git", removed: true }`; every native count 0, nothing dropped, coverage untouched); the log is then empty. The row stays `enabled`, so the next checkpoint finds no tip and RESCANS: one commit of the full current tree at the feed head (`rescanned: true`, subject `rescan: 1 document(s)`, `omgbase-rescan: ep_0:3`).

cases.name: disable-keeps-the-repository-and-a-re-enable-baselines-on-top
cases.notes: §5.9/§5.12: `history disable` closes the interval and keeps the bare repository (the log is unchanged); a checkpoint while disabled is refused (`history is disabled for this repository`); the edit at 10:05 is captured by nobody. `history enable --provider git` again at 10:06 opens a second interval and writes a new baseline commit ON TOP of the old tip (its parent), so the branch is one line and the earlier commits stay readable.

cases.name: provider-conflict
cases.notes: §5.12: one provider per repository. This repository is born with the native recorder enabled (the default); `history enable --provider git` is refused with the pinned message — switching is `history disable` then `enable --provider git`, which then baselines through git while the native rows captured earlier stay (and are no longer the repository's reader).
